payload.title: Add secure login to this application.

contract.goal: Add salted password hashing and an in-memory credential store so the app can securely store and verify user passwords. Create src/auth/password.ts exporting `hashPassword(password: string): Promise<string>` and `verifyPassword(password: string, stored: string): Promise<boolean>`, and src/auth/credentials.ts exporting class `CredentialStore` with `setPassword(userId: string, password: string): Promise<void>`, `verify(userId: string, password: string): Promise<boolean>` and `has(userId: string): boolean`. Cover both modules with vitest tests in tests/auth/password.test.ts and tests/auth/credentials.test.ts.
inputs: Repository at /Users/allenchenhan99/entente-demo/app: Node 22, TypeScript NodeNext ESM (imports must use the .js suffix), vitest 5, no lint step.
src/models/user.ts defines User/UserRepo; user ids look like 'user-1'. Credentials are keyed by user id, not stored on User.
Existing test style: tests/user.test.ts and tests/session-store.test.ts (describe/it, injected clocks, no mocks).
Consumer contract: task t-login-routes will import { CredentialStore } from '../auth/credentials.js' and call setPassword/verify/has exactly as named above.
constraints: Use only node:crypto: scrypt (async `scrypt` promisified, N=16384, r=8, p=1, keylen=64) with a fresh 16-byte random salt per hash; never MD5/SHA-only hashes and no new npm dependencies.
Stored format must be the string `scrypt$<saltHex>$<hashHex>`; verifyPassword must compare with crypto.timingSafeEqual and return false (never throw) for a malformed stored value.
setPassword must reject passwords shorter than 8 or longer than 1024 characters by throwing Error('password must be between 8 and 1024 characters').
CredentialStore.verify must return false for an unknown userId but still run one scrypt comparison against a dummy hash so timing does not reveal whether the user exists.
Never log or include plaintext passwords or hashes in error messages.
Run `npx vitest run tests/auth` and `npx tsc --noEmit` before submitting evidence; both must pass.
non_goals: Do not add HTTP routes, cookies, sessions or middleware (that is t-login-routes).
Do not add rate limiting or lockout (that is t-login-throttle).
Do not modify src/models/user.ts, src/app.ts, src/server.ts, README.md or any existing test.

acceptance_criteria.condition: hashPassword produces distinct scrypt$salt$hash strings for the same password and verifyPassword accepts the right password, rejects a wrong one and returns false on malformed input
CredentialStore sets, verifies and reports credentials, enforces the 8..1024 length rule, and returns false for unknown users
The whole project still typechecks
The existing test suite still passes
Only files under the allowed paths are changed

interpretation: Create src/auth/password.ts with hashPassword (scrypt N=16384 r=8 p=1 keylen=64, fresh 16-byte random salt, output `scrypt$<saltHex>$<hashHex>`) and verifyPassword (parses the stored string, recomputes scrypt with the stored salt, compares via crypto.timingSafeEqual, returns false rather than throwing on any malformed input).

Create src/auth/credentials.ts with class CredentialStore holding a Map<userId, storedHash>; setPassword validates the 8..1024 length rule with the exact error message and stores the hash; verify returns false for unknown users after running one scrypt comparison against a dummy hash; has reports presence synchronously.
Write tests/auth/password.test.ts and tests/auth/credentials.test.ts in the existing describe/it vitest style with no mocks, importing from '../../src/auth/*.js'.
Use only node:crypto, no new dependencies, and touch nothing outside the four allowed paths.
assumptions: hashPassword/verifyPassword themselves do not enforce the length rule; only CredentialStore.setPassword does, as stated in the constraints.
Length is measured in JavaScript string length (UTF-16 code units).
The dummy hash used for unknown users is a real scrypt hash of a random value computed once per store; verify never returns true against it.
setPassword on an existing userId overwrites the previous credential.
risks: scrypt with N=16384 costs tens of milliseconds per call, so tests that hash several times may take a few hundred ms; well within the 120s timeouts.
Length validation on UTF-16 length vs. code points could differ for astral characters; the contract does not specify, so string length is used.

interpretation: Create src/auth/throttle.ts exporting class LoginThrottle with constructor (options?: { maxAttempts?; windowMs?; lockoutMs? }, now: () => number = Date.now), defaults 5 attempts / 15 min window / 15 min lockout, and methods isBlocked, retryAfterMs, recordFailure, recordSuccess with the exact signatures in the goal.

State lives in a Map<string, entry> keyed by the caller-supplied key; each entry keeps the timestamps of recent failures (sliding window) and, once maxAttempts failures fall within windowMs, a blockedUntil = now + lockoutMs. Every lookup (isBlocked / retryAfterMs / recordFailure) prunes timestamps older than windowMs and deletes entries whose lockout has expired or that have no remaining failures, so memory stays bounded.

retryAfterMs returns blockedUntil - now while blocked and 0 otherwise; recordSuccess deletes the key entirely; the constructor validates each supplied option with Number.isFinite(x) && x > 0 and throws Error('throttle options must be finite positive numbers') otherwise, mirroring the SessionStore style.

Tests in tests/auth/throttle.test.ts use a mutable currentTime variable injected as the clock (same style as tests/session-store.test.ts), no timers, no vi.mock / fake timers, and cover blocking after maxAttempts, positive retryAfterMs while blocked, unblocking after lockoutMs, forgetting failures older than windowMs, clearing on recordSuccess, the defaults, and invalid options via it.each.
assumptions: Boundary semantics follow SessionStore: a key is blocked while now < blockedUntil and becomes unblocked at exactly now === blockedUntil (retryAfterMs 0). A failure still counts while now - failedAt <= windowMs and is forgotten once strictly older than windowMs.

recordFailure while a key is already blocked does not extend the lockout (the route calls isBlocked first, so this path is defensive). When a lockout starts, the counted failures are cleared so the key starts from zero once the lockout expires.
Only the supplied option fields are validated; omitted fields take defaults. Non-numeric values (e.g. NaN, strings at runtime) are rejected by the same Number.isFinite check.
Keys are used verbatim; normalization (lowercasing/trimming the email) is the caller's responsibility as stated in the goal.
risks: The later t-login-routes task depends on the exact API; any deviation in method names or the constructor argument order would break it, so I will keep the signatures verbatim from the goal.
Boundary choices (inclusive/exclusive at the exact expiry millisecond) are not pinned by the contract; I am choosing the SessionStore convention and documenting it in tests.

Per-key failure timestamps are capped at maxAttempts entries since a block starts at that point, so memory per key is bounded, but a large number of distinct keys with fewer than maxAttempts failures will each linger until their window expires and they are looked up again.

submission.summary: Added src/auth/throttle.ts exporting LoginThrottle with the exact contract API (constructor(options?, now = Date.now), isBlocked, retryAfterMs, recordFailure, recordSuccess). State is a Map<string, { failedAt: number[]; blockedUntil?: number }>; every lookup prunes failures older than windowMs and deletes entries whose lockout expired or that have no live failures. After maxAttempts failures within windowMs the key is blocked for lockoutMs (retryAfterMs = blockedUntil - now, 0 once now >= blockedUntil); failures recorded while blocked do not extend the lockout; recordSuccess deletes the key. Options are validated with Number.isFinite && > 0 and throw Error('throttle options must be finite positive numbers'). Tests in tests/auth/throttle.test.ts use an injected mutable clock, no timers or mocks. No dependencies added, no existing files touched.

interpretation: createApp becomes createApp(options?) with optional users/credentials/sessions/throttle/sessionTtlMs (default 12h)/secureCookies (default true); when omitted, fresh default instances are constructed so existing tests calling createApp() keep working.

POST /login validates JSON {email, password} with zod (both strings); any parse/validation failure -> 400 {error:'invalid request'}. Throttle key = email.trim().toLowerCase(); if throttle.isBlocked(key) -> 429 {error:'too many attempts'} with Retry-After = ceil(retryAfterMs/1000) seconds. Look up user by email; always call credentials.verify(user?.id ?? a dummy id, password) so unknown email costs the same as wrong password; both failures -> 401 {error:'invalid credentials'} and throttle.recordFailure(key). Success -> throttle.recordSuccess(key), sessions.create(user.id, sessionTtlMs), Set-Cookie session=<id>; Path=/; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict; Max-Age=<ttl seconds>[; Secure], body 200 {user:{id,email,name}}.

GET /me reads the 'session' cookie, calls sessions.get; a live session whose user exists returns 200 {id,email,name}; otherwise 401 {error:'not authenticated'} (unchanged). POST /logout revokes the cookie's session if present, clears the cookie with Max-Age=0 and the same flags, returns 204 always.

src/server.ts constructs CredentialStore/SessionStore/LoginThrottle/UserRepo, and if DEMO_PASSWORD is set, seeds every seeded user's password before serving requests (seeding promise awaited inside the fetch handler so startServer keeps its sync signature and return value). secureCookies = NODE_ENV !== 'development'.

Route logic lives in src/auth/routes.ts and cookie helpers in src/auth/session-cookie.ts; src/app.ts mounts them. README replaces the 'no login' sentence with docs for the three endpoints, DEMO_PASSWORD, NODE_ENV and cookie flags. tests/auth/login.test.ts covers every scenario in AC-1 using injected stores with fake clocks.
assumptions: LoginThrottle default maxAttempts is 5, so the 5th failure triggers the lockout and the 6th attempt is answered 429 before verification runs; 'six failures give 429' is satisfied by the sixth POST.
Seeded users are the two in src/models/user.ts (seededUsers); DEMO_PASSWORD must be 8-1024 chars or CredentialStore.setPassword throws, which surfaces as a server error at seed time.
Expired sessions are tested by injecting a SessionStore with a controllable clock, and throttling by a LoginThrottle with a controllable clock where needed.
Hono's built-in getCookie helper is used for cookie parsing; Set-Cookie header is assembled manually so the exact attribute order in the constraint is reproduced.
risks: If DEMO_PASSWORD is shorter than 8 characters, seeding rejects and requests fail until fixed; documented in README.
Awaiting seeding inside the fetch handler adds a one-time await on first request; negligible.
Retry-After rounding uses ceil so a client never retries too early.
